key_insight: A deep neural network predicts quantum noise figure in dual-pump fiber-optic phase-sensitive amplifiers about 400× faster than a semi-quantum calculation, with a mean absolute error of 0.0015 dB.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate enables rapid exploration of amplifier designs targeting 20 dB gain and 0.3 dB noise figure.
method: Generate simulated noise-figure data using a semi-quantum calculation framework.
Train an optimized deep neural network to predict noise figure from system parameters.
Use clustering to identify parameter regions associated with target gain and noise figure.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on numerically simulated data reports approximately 400× lower computation time and 0.0015 dB mean absolute error relative to the semi-quantum approach.
watch_item: Accuracy is established against simulations; experimental validation and reliability outside the sampled parameter space are not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Deep-learning surrogate model for rapid quantum-noise computation in dual-pump fiber-optic phase-sensitive amplifiers
